attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, summing up his own list of warnings.

semantics.note: The drafter's wording is a fair present-tense summary of the bundled list. 'Etc.' is loose, but the contract lists every element and keeps qualifiers such as 'potential' and 'threatens'.

contract.note: Testing each item for contemporary manifestations in Jan–Apr 7 2024 is an ordinary reading. It keeps threats and potential plateaus as qualified claims, so it is not stretched against Marcus. The window and the meanings of 'echo chamber' and 'undoing' are evaluator choices.

evidence.note: January 2024 study finds frequent legal hallucinations in LLMs. Supports the hallucination item.
March 2024 ARC study finds LLM weaknesses in abstraction and reasoning. Supports that item, but not a general plateau.
January 2024 revision reports failures in intuitive physics. The experiments are not precisely dated, so this is context for the physical-reasoning item.
Lab study of model collapse that also shows a mitigation. Does not show an echo chamber already contaminating the public web.
Waymo's own disclosure of an edge-case failure and fix, with service continuing. Does not settle the 'undoing' item.
Contemporary reporting on pressure to obtain training data and disputed acquisition practices. Supports the data-guzzling item; copyright legality is unsettled.
FCC release (a government statement, labelled as a company disclosure) on deception with AI-generated voices. Not shown to be LLM-driven.
Independent coding benchmark shows progress. Cautions against reading the claim as a general plateau, but does not contradict that failures existed.
Google on scaled-content abuse, whether made by humans or automation. Does not attribute it to LLMs or show a feedback mechanism.

reviews.rationale: Hallucinations, reasoning failures and the data-guzzling pressure are supported for early 2024. The evidence does not settle the echo-chamber, edge-case, plateau or LLM-driven pollution items, and none is contradicted. 'All' needs every item, so the claim as a whole is unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Naming generative AI as the dominant approach is a fair inference from the post's context. 'Monoculture' is a qualitative description; the funding comparison could in principle be tested.

contract.note: Using calendar 2023 and comparing funding across distinct technical approaches is a fair ordinary reading. The contract sets no cutoff for 'nearly', and its support condition asks for a demanding comprehensive comparison.

evidence.note: AI Index: generative AI took over a quarter of private AI investment in 2023. The rest is not broken down by technical approach.
NSF solicitation (a government agency, labelled as a company disclosure) invites neuro-symbolic and hybrid proposals. These are planned awards, not funding actually received.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no funding comparison by technical approach. The generative AI investment share and the NSF solicitation neither show nor rule out an alternative approach funded at a comparable level in 2023.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Faithful present-tense summary of all four limitations. 'Today' keeps it an observation about current systems.

contract.note: Reading the four items as substantial, continuing limitations, not total failure, is ordinary and fair. Reading 'never complete' as incomplete generalization fits the context.

evidence.note: Google admits inaccurate outputs from deployed Gemini image generation in February 2024. A documented reliability failure.
Gemma report (March 2024) discloses training on trillions of tokens. Shows heavy data needs, not acquisition pressure.
March 2024 interpretability paper: model components outside the SAEs stay uninterpretable. Also shows progress, which qualifies the opacity point.
February 2024 study: GPT models drop sharply on counterfactual analogy problems. Supports incomplete generalization.
Syndicated NYT investigation describes a desperate hunt for training data. Supports acquisition pressure tied to data needs.

reviews.rationale: Dated early-2024 evidence documents all four limitations: unreliability (Gemini), large data needs and acquisition pressure (Gemma, NYT), interpretability limits (SAE paper), and generalization failures (counterfactual analogies). Progress in interpretability qualifies the claim but does not show any limitation was broadly overcome.
